desc:
Web app testing and QA checks every feature the way real users would, then reports each problem with screenshots and steps to reproduce. Ecom Swift LLC tests on desktop and mobile browsers and, in larger packages, writes automated tests for your key flows.

## What is web app testing and QA?

Web app testing and quality assurance is the planned process of checking that software does what it should and does not break in ways users will notice. Manual testing means a person works through the app, trying normal actions and awkward ones. Automated testing means scripts repeat the important checks quickly every time the code changes.

The output is evidence: a ranked list of problems, each with the steps that cause it, so a developer can fix it without guesswork.

## Why test before a release?

The people who built an app know how it is supposed to be used, so they rarely try the things a real visitor does. A form submitted with a blank field, a back button pressed halfway through checkout or a phone held sideways can all expose faults the team never saw.

Problems found after launch cost more. Users lose data, support receives complaints and trust drops. A fresh pair of eyes before release finds those issues while they are still cheap to fix.

## How testing affects your results

Fewer defects mean fewer abandoned sign-ups, failed payments and angry messages. A clear bug list also helps your developers work in the right order, fixing what hurts users most before cosmetic problems. A written test plan makes every later release safer, because the same checks can be run again.

Automated tests add speed. Once the key flows are covered, a new release can be checked in minutes instead of a full manual pass, so the team can ship updates with less worry. Testing reduces risk, but it cannot prove an app has no bugs, and we say so plainly in our reports.

## What great testing includes

- A written list of features and user journeys to check before testing begins.
- Testing on desktop and mobile browsers, and on common phone sizes.
- Positive tests for normal use and negative tests for mistakes and odd input.
- Checks of forms, validation and error messages.
- Bug reports with a title, steps to reproduce, expected and actual results, and screenshots.
- Ranking of every problem by how much it affects users.
- A re-check after your developers have made fixes.
- Basic accessibility checks, such as keyboard use and text contrast.
- A page speed check on important pages.
- Automated tests for the flows you cannot afford to break, and a release sign-off note.

## What we do

We read your feature list, ask about the riskiest areas and build a test plan. We then work through the app on the agreed browsers and devices, logging each issue as we find it. You receive a ranked report, and after your developers fix the issues we test again to confirm.

The Basic package tests the main flows on desktop and one mobile browser and delivers a ranked bug report. Standard widens testing to more features, three browsers and two phone sizes, adds a written test plan, a re-check after fixes and checks of forms and error messages. Premium covers a large set of features with manual and automated tests, basic accessibility and speed checks, a re-check and a release sign-off note. Add-ons include extra features, more automated tests and a device pass.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Give us test accounts with a range of roles.
- Point out the areas you worry about most.
- Test on a staging copy so real data is never at risk.
- Fix the highest-ranked bugs first.
- Keep the test plan and run it again before each release.

**Avoid:**
- Testing only the path you expect users to take.
- Releasing straight after a late change without a re-check.
- Treating a short test as proof that nothing is wrong.
- Using live customer data in test accounts.
- Leaving bug reports in chat messages where they get lost.

## Who it is for

This service suits a team about to launch a new app, a business whose update keeps breaking things and a founder who has no in-house tester. It also suits agencies that want an independent check before handing a project to a client.

## What we need from you

Send a link to the app, a feature list or description of key journeys and test accounts for each role. A staging site is ideal. We never need real passwords, only test credentials made for this purpose. Any further access is given as a team or developer user.
